question_text: A studio keeps an up-to-date copy of its project files in a cloud-storage service. Describe how this can reduce interruption if its only local computer’s disk fails.
adaptation_rationale: Retain resilience reasoning by explicitly assuming cloud copy, without treating RAID/disaster recovery procedures as mandatory scope. Scenario and wording rewritten; source reasoning retained only within supported 2027 scope.
solution: A replacement internet-connected device can authenticate to the service and access the saved project files, allowing work to resume without first recovering the broken disk.

marking_points.criterion: Files remain available in independent cloud service.
Authorized replacement device retrieves/accesses current files.
Links this access to reduced need to wait for failed-disk recovery.
